params.headline: Multi-stage testing from raw material to finished bottle.
params.subhead: Every batch of private label product passes through a multi-stage testing protocol covering identity, potency, contaminants, microbials, and stability. Quality is what your brand inherits when you partner with us.

params.content:
Why testing protocols matter more than marketing claims.

Most supplement brands claim 'tested for purity and potency.' Few actually publish their testing protocols. Here's how testing works at our facility.

Every raw material is tested on receipt for identity (is this actually what was ordered) and quality (does it meet our specifications). Every batch is tested during production for potency. Every finished product is tested for contaminants, heavy metals, and microbial limits. Random samples go to third-party labs for verification.

cards.content: Every incoming raw material is tested to confirm identity before it enters production. Prevents misidentified or substituted ingredients from reaching your customers.

items.answer: Identity testing confirms the raw material we receive is actually what the supplier says it is. For botanical ingredients especially, identity testing prevents accidentally or intentionally using a substitute ingredient. We use HPLC (high-performance liquid chromatography), microscopy, and other methods depending on the material.
items.question: What does identity testing actually mean?

items.answer: Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury) on every batch where applicable. Microbials (yeast, mold, E. coli, salmonella, total plate count) for ingredients where microbial contamination is a risk. Pesticide residues on botanicals from sources where pesticides are a concern. Residual solvents on extracts. Allergens for facility cross-contact concerns.
items.question: What contaminants do you test for?

items.answer: Yes. Stability testing is required to support shelf life claims (usually 2-3 years from manufacture date for supplements). We do real-time and accelerated stability testing on representative batches to validate claims. Custom formulations require dedicated stability testing before launch.
items.question: Do you do stability testing for shelf life claims?

items.answer: A Certificate of Analysis (CoA) is a document we provide for every batch documenting test results: identity confirmation, potency (active ingredient quantity), contaminant test results, microbial counts (where applicable), and physical specifications (color, appearance, weight). CoAs travel with every batch you receive.
